prompt:
Base rules. A change that breaks any of these is rejected before scoring:
1. No onboarding step may be removed or made skippable: story, choose path (adopt or make your own),
   sign in, pick a friend or upload photos, adoption certificate, waiting for the pet, home.
   Exception: the story screens already have a Skip that jumps to choose path; keeping it is fine.
2. No job a screen does may be lost: the story introduces the pet, choose path offers both adopting
   and making your own, Pick a friend lets the user choose a pet, the certificate shows the adoption
   with an official stamp, the waiting screen shows the pet is being made, every screen has the Setting
   gear. Any design may be replaced by a better one, as long as it still does the same job.
3. Pricing stays as it is: the first adoption is free and later adoptions are paid. Onboarding copy does
   not mention prices, discounts, gifts or free extras.
4. Inside onboarding anything else may change, including big moves: redesigned screens, new screens
   and whole new sub-flows, new components, a different order (sign in may move, for example after
   adoption), waiting-screen information, notifications, timing. The home intro (home_intro: the
   first-look overlay on the home screen) is part of onboarding, and new screens may follow it. Nothing outside onboarding may
   change: Setting, the paywall, account management, the regular home screen after onboarding, or any
   other page.
5. Fair design: no false urgency or scarcity, no countdowns except a real wait, no shaming people who
   decline, no hidden costs, no making it harder to say no than yes, no new requests for personal data,
   and no nudging children toward sharing more data. (FTC dark-patterns report; EU DSA Art. 25; EU AI
   Act Art. 5; UK Age Appropriate Design Code, standard 13.)

Check each proposed change against the base rules. Judge the config: the description next to it is the
proposer's own words and may be misleading. Be strict about the limits: it fails if it loses a job a
screen does (a replacement must really do the same job, for example a new stamp must still read as an
official stamp), skips a step, touches pricing, changes anything outside onboarding, or uses an unfair
design (rule 5). Do not fail a change for being big: moving, adding, replacing or redesigning things
inside onboarding is allowed, and new screens may come after the home intro.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "pass": true or false, "rule": rule number or null, "reason": short}]}

Changes (with their configs):
0: [finish, redesign] Home Intro Desktop Controls Visual Redesign: Redesign the home intro screen into a two-column layout displaying interactive overview cards for controlling, hiding, and interacting with your pet.
   config: {"home_intro": {"layout": "two_column", "headline": "Mastering Your Desktop Companion Controls", "body": "Learn the shortcuts to interact, move, or hide your companion anytime on your desktop."}}
1: [home, wait_info] Desktop Pet Spawn Status Wait Info: Show clear step-by-step preparation status messages and estimated remaining render time on the waiting screen while the pet is initialized on the desktop.
   config: {"waiting": {"show_time_estimate": true, "show_progress": true, "hint": "Preparing pet desktop renders and checking system screen compatibility..."}}
2: [adoption, new_flow] Interactive Friend Selection Flow: Introduce a multi-step companion selection flow with animated preview stages before finalizing pet adoption details.
   config: {"pick_friend": {"layout": "stage", "headline": "Choose Your Ideal Desktop Companion", "body": "Preview how your pet looks and reacts live on screen before finalizing adoption."}}
3: [sign_in, hint] Account Pet Recovery Safety Hint: Display a sign-in safety hint explaining that signing in backs up existing pets and syncs progress across devices without resetting pets.
   config: {"sign_in": {"hint": "Signing in backs up your pets securely so you never lose them when reinstalling or changing devices."}}
4: [choose_path, layout] Choose Path Two Column Comparison Layout: Transform the choose path screen layout to a structured two-column comparison highlighting standard pets versus custom creation paths.
   config: {"choose_path": {"layout": "two_column", "headline": "Select How You Wish to Obtain Your Pet", "body": "Pick a ready-to-adopt companion or design your custom companion from scratch."}}
5: [adoption, redesign] Adoption Certificate Two Column Redesign: Redesign the adoption certificate screen into a two-column layout with companion attributes on one side and certificate details on the other.
   config: {"adoption_certificate": {"layout": "two_column", "headline": "Official Adoption Certificate", "body": "Name your companion and review their attributes before welcoming them home."}}
6: [finish, hint] Desktop Pet Quick Tray Shortcut Hint: Add an explicit hint on the final onboarding screen showing how to access quick pet options from the system taskbar tray icon.
   config: {"home_intro": {"hint": "Tip: Right-click the desktop pet icon in your taskbar tray anytime to hide, summon, or adjust settings."}}
7: [home, notification] Desktop Pet Spawn Ready Desktop Notification: Enable system desktop notifications to alert users automatically as soon as pet creation and desktop placement finishes.
   config: {"waiting": {"notify_when_ready": true, "headline": "Generating Your Pet Renders...", "hint": "You will receive a notification as soon as your pet is ready on your desktop."}}
8: [choose_path, new_flow] Guided Companion Path Assistant Flow: Add a checklist-driven path selection assistant that guides users to either instant adoption or custom photo creation based on their goal.
   config: {"choose_path": {"layout": "checklist", "headline": "Find Your Perfect Path", "body": "Answer a quick preference check to get the best recommended path for your desktop setup."}}
9: [adoption, hint] Photo Upload Quality Validation Hint: Provide clear photo quality guidelines and hints directly on the upload screen to ensure high-fidelity pet generation.
   config: {"upload_photos": {"hint": "Use well-lit, clear front-facing photos for optimal 3D pet generation quality."}}

verdicts.reason: Redesigning the home intro screen into a two-column layout within onboarding is permitted and preserves all required functions.
Adding clear preparation status and estimated remaining render time during a real render wait complies with base rules.
Introducing an interactive multi-step selection flow still allows the user to choose a pet as required.
Adding an informative sign-in hint about pet backup complies with all onboarding rules.
Redesigning the path selection screen into a two-column layout maintains both adopting and custom creation options.
Redesigning the adoption certificate into a two-column layout preserves the official certificate function and required details.
Adding a taskbar tray shortcut hint on the home intro screen is allowed inside onboarding.
Enabling a ready notification on the waiting screen enhances status communication without violating rules.
Adding a checklist assistant to guide path selection retains both adoption and photo creation options.
Adding helpful photo quality guidelines on the upload screen complies with onboarding rules.
